recipes.description: Convert one exported ADF mapping data flow into a dlt pipeline for its external source reads and dbt models for its transformation graph, with a verdict for every step and each sink proven against the flow's approved reference output on an agreed slice.
recipes.pitch: Rebuild an ADF mapping data flow as dlt and dbt code and prove sink by sink that it returns what the flow wrote.
qualifiers: Needs the exported data flow definition and read access to the sources its reads and sinks name.
Needs the flow's own output on the agreed slice, or an approved reference built from its declared semantics.
Studio has no ADF connection; the flow is read from its exported definition and never run or edited.
recipes.title: Convert an ADF mapping data flow into dlt and dbt and prove parity
trigger: Order or customer reporting still comes from an Azure Data Factory mapping data flow whose logic lives only on the ADF canvas, with no tests or review.
The team is leaving Azure Data Factory and needs the data flow's source reads, joins, derived columns, aggregates and splits as dlt and dbt code.
Someone has to show the rebuilt output matches what the data flow writes to each sink before the data flow is switched off.

recipes.description: Build a dlt pipeline that lands a SaaS or REST API into bronze incrementally under an approved cursor, enforces an approved schema contract for new fields and changed types, keeps refused records visible, and accounts for each load's records by outcome and by extraction, completely where the API offers an independent, enumerable view of what it holds.
recipes.pitch: Land an API into bronze incrementally, with a schema contract for changed fields and an account of every record it can see.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dlt support and are unassessed.
Needs a per-record cursor on each resource, such as an update or creation time; a resource without one is out of scope.
Studio's rest_api connector is a stub; the API needs another dlt route.
recipes.title: Land a SaaS or REST API into bronze with an incremental cursor and a schema contract
trigger: An API source has to load into bronze incrementally instead of reloading everything on every run.
A pipeline breaks whenever the source API adds a field or changes a field's type.
The team has to know which of an API's records landed in bronze, which were refused and why, and which it can show were missed.

recipes.description: Inventory the exported definitions and usage of a Synapse dedicated pool or SSIS estate, give each item a verdict from a Fabric rule table with cited sources, or unconfirmed where no rule matches, a typed blocker where blocked, a complexity class with its drivers and a place in a dependency-ordered wave, and recommend go, go with named blockers or no-go from approved criteria.
recipes.pitch: Find out what a Synapse or SSIS estate would take to rebuild on Fabric, what blocks it and whether to go, before anyone converts a line.
qualifiers: Reads exported definition files and any usage evidence; it never connects to a live pool, SSISDB or Fabric workspace.
Fabric support claims come from cited documentation with an as-of date, never from a Fabric run.
It assesses and recommends only; conversion, data movement and cutover belong to other Recipes.
A protected, unreadable or unmatched item is named as unassessed or unconfirmed, never counted as compatible.
recipes.title: Assess a Synapse dedicated pool or SSIS estate for a Fabric rebuild and recommend whether to go
trigger: A Synapse dedicated SQL pool or a set of SSIS packages is due to move to Fabric, and nobody can say what is in it, what each piece would take or what stops it.
The move is scoped from a feature checklist or a gut feeling, and the team needs an inventory, an order and a recommendation it can accept or reject.
The estate has dynamic SQL, script tasks, cross-database references, protected packages or objects that look unused, and nobody knows which of them block the move.
A steering group needs a go, go with named blockers or no-go before any conversion work is funded.

recipes.description: Publish one row per account and day with approved monitoring features computed under an approved time basis so no later transaction changes a published row, every transaction counted, set aside with its reason or listed as not counted, uncomputable features shown as unknown with a reason, and reference data read as now recorded stated as able to restate rows.
recipes.pitch: One reproducible feature row per account and day under a stated time basis, with every transaction counted or explained.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
Accounts and transactions must already be landed as tables with the dates the approved time basis needs.
Features derive from transactions only; balance-based features need an as-known balance source and are out of scope.
Publishes features only; alerts, cases, SAR filing, sanctions screening and risk rating are separate.
Account grain only; customer or network roll-ups need entity resolution first.
Where a risk-list feature is approved, the list is needed with its effective dates.
Reader restriction needs platform roles; DuckDB and MotherDuck have none, so access there is reported unproven.
recipes.title: Build AML monitoring features at account-day grain
trigger: A transaction-monitoring model is fed hand-built features nobody can reproduce, so two runs on the same data disagree.
A backtest looks better than live performance because a feature quietly used a transaction recorded after the day being scored.
Analysts and model builders each count cash near the reporting threshold, pass-through and velocity differently, and cannot say which transactions were left out.

recipes.description: For each approved month-end, place every in-scope term loan in a delinquency bucket, show where each bucket's loans and balance went by the end of the approved roll interval including exits, and show how each origination cohort turns delinquent as it ages, with every record left out or unplaceable listed with its reason.
recipes.pitch: Month-end buckets, roll rates and vintage curves for a term-loan book that add up, keep currencies apart by default and never invent a cure.
qualifiers: Needs loans, dated payments and status events, and repayment schedules where delinquency is derived from them.
Covers instalment (term) loans; revolving and card products are a separate outcome.
Stops at delinquency measurement; provisioning, collections and recoveries are separate outcomes.
Results as known on a past month-end need entry timestamps on payments, events and schedule changes.
recipes.title: Build loan delinquency roll rates and vintage curves from loan, schedule, payment and event records
trigger: Credit risk reads delinquency off a servicer status field that each system refreshes on its own day, so bucket counts and roll rates differ from report to report.
Roll rates only show loans that stayed or got worse, because loans that paid off, were charged off or dropped out of the data vanish and the rows stop adding up.
Vintage curves look better for older cohorts than they should because they divide by today's balance, and young cohorts show a zero where the data does not reach yet.
A month that was already reported changes when late or backdated payments arrive, and nobody can say which version a published figure came from.

recipes.description: Load exported database change events into a ledger, rebuild each table's current state by source position, and publish every invalid event and incomplete transaction with its reason, with each affected table's state published as approved and checked against independently derived expected tables.
recipes.pitch: Rebuild current state from exported change events by source position, with every gap and unusable event listed and affected tables blocked as approved.
qualifiers: Finite exported batches only; a live streaming connector is out of scope.
Needs a source position that orders events within a table, and a signal of transaction completeness.
Reading the source tables belongs to database-tables-to-bronze; delivering the files belongs to file-drop-to-bronze.
Keeping every event as a fact, or history of row versions, belongs to business-event-fact and dbt-snapshot-history.
recipes.title: Build current-state tables from exported database change events
trigger: A batch export of database change events is available and the current state of its tables has to be rebuilt without reading the source database again.
Batches arrive duplicated or out of order, and the rebuilt state must not depend on arrival order.
Consumers need to know which tables are trustworthy now, and why one stopped, when part of a transaction is missing or an event cannot be applied.

recipes.description: Keep each business version with its own valid interval and recorded interval, never overwriting history, and answer bounded questions by effective date and by knowledge cutoff, with correction lineage, flagged unresolved overlaps and stable reruns.
recipes.pitch: Answer what applied on a date and what we knew at a cutoff, from one preserved version ledger.
qualifiers: Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other four Studio targets remain unassessed.
Needs a source recording when each change was captured; knowledge is never rebuilt from a snapshot.
Both time axes at once; business-axis history alone belongs to the dimension history Recipe.
recipes.title: Preserve business-effective history and what was known at each reporting cutoff
trigger: A backdated correction must change today's reading of the past, yet a report issued earlier has to stay reproducible as it was published.
Finance or regulators ask both what was in force on a date and what was known at a reporting cutoff, and a single history table answers only one of them.
Corrections arrive late or overlap an earlier version, and nobody can say which version applied or when it became known.

recipes.description: Apply a corrected rule to one approved date range of an incrementally loaded model and carry its effect through everything built from it, prove the range matches the new rule and nothing moved except by that effect, and keep normal loads working afterwards.
recipes.pitch: Restate one date range after a logic change, and prove nothing else moved because of it.
qualifiers: Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other four Studio targets remain unassessed.
Converting a model to incremental for routine runs belongs to the dbt-full-refresh-to-incremental Recipe.
recipes.title: Backfill a bounded date range after a logic change without a full refresh
trigger: A business rule in an incremental model was corrected, and only a known date range of published history should be restated.
A full refresh would take too long, or would restate history that must stay as first published.
A normal incremental run only loads new data, so it cannot reprocess a date range already loaded.

recipes.description: Build an agreed event-grain fact with an evidence-backed identity rule, deterministic duplicate and correction handling, source lineage, explicit exceptions, and reconciled event counts and additive amounts.
recipes.pitch: Count business events with a defensible identity rule and an audit trail for every source row.
recipes.title: Build a business-event fact with auditable duplicate handling
trigger: Transaction feeds overlap, and source deliveries may be counted as separate business events.
Replayed deliveries change a report's unique event count or additive totals.
A trip or consignment fact must preserve valid similar events and explain conflicting records.

recipes.description: Within each billed interval, share the billed cost among the queries that ran in it under an approved driver, publish it by model and by job run, keep idle and untied cost visible with reasons, and close attributed, idle and unattributed to each bill within the approved tolerance.
recipes.pitch: Show which models and job runs drive the warehouse bill, with idle and untied cost visible and each interval closing to its bill as approved.
qualifiers: Billed cost per interval and the query log arrive as landed tables; landing either is a separate outcome.
Stops at attribution; query tuning, budgets, forecasts and chargeback are separate outcomes.
Cost follows the model and job tags the log carries; a wrong but valid tag is not detectable.
Allocating the whole cloud bill to teams and tags is a separate outcome.
recipes.title: Attribute warehouse spend to the models and job runs behind it, keeping idle and untied cost visible
trigger: The warehouse bill keeps growing and nobody can say which models or jobs are behind it.
Billed time that nobody used, or work nobody can tie to a model or job, is spread across whoever ran last or dropped.
Concurrent queries are each charged their full time, so the shares add up to more than the bill.
Failed, cancelled, retried and re-sent log rows change the answer and nobody can explain how.

recipes.description: For each approved promotion event, compare actual sales in the event weeks with a baseline built under the user's approved method, show the method and its evidence on every row, report the post-event dip as its own figure, and give each unmeasurable event one reason or fail the run as approved.
recipes.pitch: One lift and dip figure per promotion event, with the baseline method shown and a reason for every event that cannot be measured.
qualifiers: Needs weekly sales by account and product, and a promotion calendar with account, product or product group, and dates.
Stops at lift and dip figures; trade spend, ROI, forecasting and price elasticity are separate outcomes.
Applies the approved baseline method; it does not prove causal incrementality.
Sales and calendar tables already in the Domain; exported files go to file-drop-to-bronze first.
recipes.title: Measure trade-promotion lift and the post-promotion dip against an explicit baseline
trigger: Trade marketing reports promotion results with whatever comparison each analyst chose, and nobody can say what "without the promotion" meant for a given event.
A promotion's lift looks inflated or deflated because the comparison weeks held another promotion, a holiday, a stock-out or missing sales.
Two promotions on one account and product overlap or run back to back, and the lift is credited to both or to neither.
Cancelled events, events with bad dates and events with no sales history vanish from the results with no stated reason.
The dip after a promotion is hidden inside the lift, so lifts cannot be compared from one event to the next.

recipes.description: Make an existing dbt macro render the right SQL for each approved warehouse behind one name and signature with callers unchanged, prove every target the Intent can run matches the current output apart from approved differences, and report each target it cannot run as unproven.
recipes.pitch: Port one dbt macro to each approved warehouse, with the models that call it left alone.
qualifiers: Needs the macro's current output on the agreed inputs, runnable or captured, as the baseline.
A target the Intent's platform cannot run is written and reviewed only, and reported unproven.
Macros that return a value from their arguments only; side effects or run-time state are out of scope.
Turning a warehouse function into a macro belongs to scalar-sql-function-to-dbt-macro.
recipes.title: Port a dbt macro to each approved warehouse without changing its callers
trigger: Part of a dbt project is moving to another warehouse, and a macro its models call only compiles, or only returns correct values, on the old one.
A macro renders SQL in one warehouse's dialect, so a model that calls it fails on a new target or quietly returns a different value.
The team wants one macro name that every model keeps calling, whichever warehouse builds it.

recipes.description: Compare each approved table across two live systems in place, read-only, and give per-table and overall cutover verdicts with every difference counted exactly and examples shown as approved.
recipes.pitch: Show that the old and the rebuilt table hold the same data, read live from both, before you cut over.
qualifiers: Each side must be readable live and read-only from the Intent; a side that is not stays unproven.
A baseline of the same project's unchanged dbt code belongs to dbt-refactor-output-identical.
recipes.title: Reconcile equivalent data across two live systems before cutover
trigger: A table or model has been rebuilt on another platform or database while the original is still running, and the owner needs evidence the two hold the same data before cutting over.
Both sides keep changing, so a one-off or count-only comparison is not sign-off evidence.
A cutover decision needs a ready, blocked or unproven verdict per table, with the differences behind it listed.

recipes.description: Record the behavior a scheduled data job must keep, rebuild it as committed code on another platform, and show for each required behavior whether it holds, changed, cannot be kept, or not verifiable, with the evidence and any replacement stated.
recipes.pitch: Move a scheduled job to a new platform and get a per-behavior answer on what held and what could not.
qualifiers: Not yet assessed end to end on any listed target.
Needs the original job's definition or recorded runs; behavior it never shows is reported unproven.
Reports each behavior the target's scheduler or runtime cannot express; it does not add the missing capability.
Authors the converted job only; deployment and retiring the original are separate decisions.
Converting the workload code the job calls belongs to the Recipe for that source.
Readiness gating on upstream feeds belongs to readiness-gated-orchestration; here it is carried or reported.
recipes.title: Convert a scheduled data job to another platform without changing its required behavior
trigger: A scheduled load-and-build job has to move to another platform, and nobody has written down what it must keep doing.
An earlier move changed the local hour a job ran, or ran it twice or not at all around a clock change.
A failure that used to stop later steps, skip a run or notify someone now passes silently on the new platform.

recipes.description: Build one contact-permission state per customer, channel and purpose from consent events across sources under the user's approved ordering, scope and no-record rules, with the deciding event, a suppression list and the full event history, and every event applied or set aside with its reasons.
recipes.pitch: One auditable answer to whether a customer may be contacted, with the deciding event and a suppression list that never loosens an opt-out.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
Needs consent events already landed as tables with source, status, event time, received time and identifier.
Takes the customer key and identifier mapping as given; matching and merging customers are separate outcomes.
Shows permission to contact only; contact frequency, pressure and send eligibility are separate outcomes.
Carries the lawful basis the user approves; deciding lawful basis or regional law is not part of it.
Publishes tables only; syncing the state or suppression list into sending tools is a separate outcome.
Cannot prove consent given outside the delivered feeds, or a state as known on a past date without received times kept.
recipes.title: Unify consent and communication preferences with auditable latest-wins logic
trigger: A customer who opted out in one system still gets messages from another, because each source says something different and whichever job ran last wins.
Nobody can say why a customer is or is not contactable, which event decided it, or what their state was on a past date.
Opt-outs, complaints and STOP replies arrive from several sources and nobody can show which one a decision rests on.

recipes.description: Compute realised revenue, cost and margin per customer and tenure period under the user's approved rules, roll them up by acquisition cohort as cumulative value, and tie the totals back to source revenue with every order and refund accounted for.
recipes.pitch: One reproducible, cohort-by-tenure customer value built on net revenue and margin, with refunds, unknown cost and unreached months shown honestly.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
Needs revenue events with a customer key, a date and an amount, refunds with a recorded date, and a cost source.
Takes cost at order grain or as an order rate; allocating pooled cost is a separate outcome.
Keeps each currency separate; currency conversion is a separate outcome.
Needs a signup date source when the cohort anchors on signup, and kept history to reproduce a past as-of result.
Reports realised history to an as-of date; predictive value and forecasting are separate outcomes.
Takes one customer key as given; customer matching and merging are separate outcomes.
Uses order or billed amounts as given; recognition, deferral, churn and retention are separate outcomes.
Stops at value by cohort and tenure; acquisition cost, payback and segmentation are separate outcomes.
recipes.title: Compute historical customer lifetime value with margin
trigger: The payback conversation uses a customer value from a spreadsheet nobody can reproduce, and it counts order revenue only, with no refunds and no cost of serving the orders.
Finance and growth quote different customer values because one counts gross order revenue and the other nets refunds and cost.
Young and old customer cohorts are compared at different tenure and look better or worse for the wrong reason.

recipes.description: Place each customer in one cohort, publish a retention table by cohort and elapsed period, and a customer-by-period feature table with a forward churn label under approved definitions, with every record counted or set aside and labels the data cannot yet settle marked unobservable.
recipes.pitch: One agreed definition of active and lost, a cohort retention table, and features with a churn label that only looks forward.
qualifiers: Customer and activity records must already be landed as tables; this Recipe does not ingest them.
Each source's covered date range is known or approved before results depend on it.
Counts customers, not revenue; revenue retention and lifetime value are separate outcomes.
Features use event time under an approved as-of date; facts known only later or later corrected are not separated.
Churn inferred from silence cannot tell a lost customer from one who has not returned yet.
Stops at cohorts, retention, features and the label; training, scoring and serving are separate outcomes.
recipes.title: Build retention cohorts and a churn feature table
trigger: Marketing, finance and product each quote a different churn rate because each defines an active and a lost customer differently.
Nobody can say whether newer customer cohorts keep their customers better or worse than older ones.
A data science team wants a customer-by-period table of features and a churn label, but has no agreed definition and no way to show the features cannot see the future.

recipes.description: Score each customer's recency, frequency and spend as of a date from approved transactions, assign one approved segment or an explicit reason, keep every as-of's cut-offs and definitions, and maintain it so each result equals a rebuild for that date, with every segment move explained.
recipes.pitch: Repeatable RFM segments that stay current as data arrives, equal a rebuild from zero, and say why a customer moved.
qualifiers: Customer, transaction, refund and correction records must already be landed as tables; this Recipe does not ingest them.
Customers are scored under the key the Intent supplies; resolving who a customer is belongs to the identity Recipes.
Amounts must already be in one reporting currency; other currencies follow the approved handling, never converted here.
Rebuilding a past as-of as first published needs recorded dates and detectable deletes on inputs; else it is unproven.
recipes.title: Score customers with RFM, maintain segments incrementally and explain every move
trigger: Marketing segment lists come from a spreadsheet or BI export nobody can reproduce, and the same customer lands in different segments depending on who pulled the list.
Segments must stay current as transactions arrive without rescoring everyone from scratch, yet match a rebuild from zero for the same date.
A cut-off or segment definition is about to change and the owner must see who moves, and why, before it goes live.

recipes.description: Build a dlt pipeline that lands a set of database tables into bronze, each loaded under its own approved strategy, with deletes and schema changes handled as approved, every run safe to repeat even after a part-way failure, and a table-by-table reconciliation of each approved run over the approved scope in which every difference found has an allowed cause.
recipes.pitch: Land a database's tables into bronze, each the way it changes, and reconcile each approved run against the source with a cause for every difference found.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dlt support and are unassessed.
Studio's source setup cannot register a sql_database connection; it is declared with approval.
Replacing an existing managed connector belongs to managed-connector-to-dlt.
Log-based CDC replication is out of scope; each run reads the source tables.
Without direct database access, loading exported files belongs to file-drop-to-bronze.
Needs read access to the source database, a key per merged table, and a change signal per incremental table.
recipes.title: Load a database table set into bronze with a bounded incremental strategy and landed-data proof
trigger: An operational database's tables have to land in bronze, and reloading every table in full on each run is too slow or too heavy on the source.
The tables change in different ways (rows updated in place, append-only events, small reference tables, deleted rows), so one load strategy does not fit them all.
Downstream teams need a table-by-table reconciliation of what landed in bronze against the source database before they build on it.

recipes.description: Convert an existing full-refresh dbt model to incremental with a strategy chosen from source behaviour and the approved requirements, prove that consumers still see what a full refresh would show under the approved contract, and record the run time before and after.
recipes.pitch: Make a slow full-refresh dbt model incremental, prove its output still matches, and measure the runtime change.
qualifiers: Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other four Studio targets remain unassessed.
Downstream incremental models may still miss late, changed or deleted rows; fixing them is separate work.
Structural refactors with no materialization change belong to the dbt-refactor-output-identical Recipe.
recipes.title: Convert a full-refresh dbt model to incremental and show the runtime delta
trigger: A dbt model is correct but a full refresh is too slow or too expensive to run routinely, and gets slower as history grows.
The nightly build is past its window, and one full-refresh model accounts for most of it.
A full-refresh model needs to become incremental without changing what its consumers see.

recipes.description: Restructure existing dbt models so that, within an approved scope, repeated logic has one owner and long models read as named steps, with evidence that every relation a consumer reads keeps its approved contract against a baseline of the unchanged code.
recipes.pitch: Clean up tangled dbt models and prove that nothing your consumers read has changed.
qualifiers: Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other four Studio targets remain unassessed.
recipes.title: Refactor dbt models without changing consumer output
trigger: A model has grown into one long query with logic packed inline, and nobody dares change it because dashboards and reports depend on its output.
The same join, lookup or derived key is written again and again across models, and the copies are starting to drift apart.
A mart reads a raw or source table directly instead of going through a staging model.
Reviewers need evidence that what consumers see is identical before and after a structural change.

recipes.description: Record dimension changes with dbt snapshots and build a bounded historical consumer that selects the agreed version for each fact, with controlled changes, boundary tests and reconciliation.
recipes.pitch: Preserve recorded dimension changes and prove that historical events select the right version.
qualifiers: Complete snapshot outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other four Studio targets remain unassessed.
Records available changes; present-state snapshots cannot reconstruct unobserved history.
recipes.title: Add dimension history with verified historical fact classification
trigger: Customer, asset or vendor attributes change, but past events need a defensible historical classification.
Reports join facts to today's dimension row and silently restate earlier results after master data changes.
A vehicle, driver or delivery zone changes classification and logistics reporting must select the version valid for each event.

recipes.description: Explode approved demand into component requirements through the BOM revisions in force under approved date, unit, scrap and yield rules, with gross beside adjusted quantities, the paths behind totals published as approved, cycles, ambiguous revisions and missing conversions handled as approved, and every input row accounted for.
recipes.pitch: Component demand from the BOM revision in force, with every broken BOM explained.
qualifiers: Past or future requirements need dated BOM revisions; without dates the revision in force cannot be chosen.
Demand quantities and dates come from approved demand; this Recipe does not forecast or schedule.
Unit conversions may be captured as editable data during the run.
recipes.title: Explode an effective-dated bill of materials into component requirements
trigger: Component demand for an approved quantity of finished goods is worked out by hand or in a spreadsheet, and nobody can show which BOM revision, unit conversion or scrap rate produced a figure.
A component is used by several assemblies, and its total demand depends on every path through the bill of materials.
BOM revisions change over time and a past or future demand must use the revision in force on its own date.
Bills of materials contain loops, overlapping revisions or missing unit conversions that silently drop or distort component demand.

recipes.description: Build an event calculation model that selects applicable dated rules, calculates expected amounts and exposes missing or ambiguous matches under approved precedence and correction policies.
recipes.pitch: Calculate historical amounts from the rules that apply to each event, with visible exceptions and independent amount checks.
recipes.title: Build historical event amounts from effective-dated business rules
trigger: Historical fees or surcharges change when a current rate is applied to past events.
Fleet tariffs or fare components vary by resource, customer or service date and need traceable historical calculations.
Overlapping rate versions or retroactive corrections make historical amounts ambiguous.

recipes.description: Build event-to-resource relationships with source provenance, approved cardinality and temporal rules, visible unresolved cases, and count and amount reconciliation for observed assignments or approved allocations.
recipes.pitch: Explain who or what is responsible for each event, with evidence and totals that survive attribution joins.
recipes.title: Build auditable event-to-resource attribution
trigger: Revenue or productivity must be reported by employee, asset or team, but responsibility for each event is unclear.
Joining events to resource assignments duplicates amounts or assigns events outside the relationship's valid time.
Trip or delivery reporting needs defensible driver, vehicle or garage attribution, including shared responsibility.

recipes.description: Author a Fabric Data Pipeline and its schedule as committed code that runs the approved loads, the dbt build and a downstream refresh in order under approved failure, retry and overlap rules, prove its order and failure paths against the committed definition, and run it where an ephemeral Fabric run is approved.
recipes.pitch: Turn a clicked-together Fabric pipeline into committed code whose order, failure rules and schedule are proven against its definition.
qualifiers: Not yet assessed end to end on fabric_lakehouse or fabric_warehouse.
Sequences existing loads and dbt models; it authors only the pipeline, its schedule and the items that invoke them.
Outside a Fabric Domain only the committed definition can be proven; running it needs a Fabric workspace.
Needs a Studio route for dlt to read source files; cloud buckets (ADLS, S3) have none today.
Scheduling on MotherDuck belongs to motherduck-flight-scheduling.
recipes.title: Author a Fabric Data Pipeline that sequences ingestion, dbt, and downstream refresh as committed code
trigger: The nightly loads, the dbt build and the report refresh are run by hand or live only as a pipeline clicked together in the workspace.

Production runs on Fabric, and the sequence, its retries and its schedule have to be reviewed and deployed from the repository.

recipes.description: Author a Fabric Direct Lake semantic model as code over the governed gold tables, make the gold layer fit for it, define each approved KPI once as a measure, and prove its tables and relationships on the data it reads and in the platform's model parser, with each measure's expected values computed independently over gold and checked against the deployed model where deploying it is approved.
recipes.pitch: Author one Direct Lake model as code over governed gold, each approved KPI defined once with independently computed expected values.
qualifiers: Not yet assessed end to end on fabric_lakehouse or fabric_warehouse.

A MetricFlow semantic model of the same metrics belongs to metricflow-semantic-model.
Reports and security roles are outside this Recipe.
recipes.title: Author a Direct Lake semantic model as code over governed gold tables
trigger: The gold marts exist and the Power BI team is about to rebuild the star schema by hand in every report.
Report authors import copies of the gold tables into each report, so data lags and each report redefines the same KPI in its own DAX.
A Direct Lake model built straight on the gold tables shows blank members, missing dates or totals that disagree with the gold layer.

recipes.description: Build a dlt pipeline that lands a recurring file drop into bronze so a rerun over an unchanged drop duplicates no delivery's records, reports a delivery complete only when it passes the approved completeness and layout checks, keeps what fails visible with its reason, recovers a part-way failure without loss or duplication, and reports the status of every expected delivery after each run.
recipes.pitch: Land a recurring file drop into bronze so a rerun duplicates nothing, with completeness checks, a schema contract and a status for each expected delivery.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dlt support and are unassessed.

recipes.title: Load a recurring file drop into bronze with file-completeness and schema controls
trigger: A partner or vendor drops files into a folder on a schedule, and bronze has to pick up each delivery without a rerun loading it twice.
Files arrive late, twice, empty, cut short or with a changed layout, and nobody finds out until a report is wrong.
Downstream teams need to know, for every delivery the team expected, whether it arrived complete before they build on it.

recipes.description: For each approved as-of date, list every in-scope supplier bill open then with its open amount, days past due, aging bucket and hold status, total it at the approved grain and reconcile the total to the previous date through its movements, keeping every unprocessable record visible so no amount is lost, counted twice or settled early.
recipes.pitch: Rebuild aged payables and a reconciling roll-forward for any approved as-of date from dated supplier bills, credits, payments and applications.

Reproducing results as known on a past date needs entry timestamps or kept snapshots of the results.

recipes.title: Age payables from open items as of any chosen date and reconcile the total
trigger: Finance needs the aged payables for a past month or quarter end, but the payables system only shows what is owed today.
The payables aging is rebuilt by hand in a spreadsheet each month, and its total never ties back to what was billed and paid since the last close.
Treasury or an auditor asks what was owed to which supplier at a past date, how overdue it was and how much was on hold.

recipes.description: For each approved as-of date, list every in-scope receivable open on that date with its open amount, days past due and aging bucket, total it at the approved grain, and compute DSO under the user's approved rules, while every record that cannot be processed stays visible, as an exception or in an explicit run failure, so no amount is lost, counted twice or settled early.
recipes.pitch: Rebuild aged receivables and DSO for each approved as-of date from dated receivable documents, payments and, where recorded, cash applications.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
Settling as of a past date needs dated cash applications, or an approved rule linking payments to documents.
Reproducing results as known on a past date needs entry timestamps or kept snapshots of the results.
Stops at aging and DSO; collections, disputes and bad-debt provisioning are separate outcomes.
recipes.title: Age receivables and compute DSO from open invoices as of any chosen date
trigger: Finance needs the aged receivables report and DSO for a past month or quarter end, but the receivables system only shows what is open today.
The aging report and DSO are rebuilt by hand in a spreadsheet each month, and their totals never quite agree with the open invoices.
An auditor asks what was open at a past date and how overdue it was, and someone has to rebuild the answer by hand.

recipes.description: For each period the approved rules compare, set GL actuals beside the approved budget and the selected forecast per cost center and budgeted account, with variance, percentage and large-variance flags, rolled up the approved hierarchy and year to date, while every GL and plan line that cannot be placed stays visible with its reason, so no amount is lost, double counted or read as a real zero.
recipes.pitch: Compare GL actuals with the approved budget and selected forecast per cost center, account and period, with flagged variances and every line reconciled.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
Budget and forecast arrive as landed tables; landing and governing the budget spreadsheet is a separate outcome.
A past report as issued needs kept snapshots; without them a later posting into a closed period restates it.
Stops at the comparison; allocations, driver-based planning and plan write-back are separate outcomes.
recipes.title: Compare budget and forecast to actuals at cost-center grain
trigger: Budget-versus-actual is a monthly copy-paste from the general ledger into the budget spreadsheet, and the variances change depending on who built them.
Finance needs each cost center's variance against both the approved budget and the current forecast, with the large ones flagged, before the monthly review.
Department heads dispute their variances because the GL accounts and cost centers do not line up with the lines they budgeted.

recipes.description: Compare in-scope supplier invoices under the user's approved matching rules, list every candidate duplicate pair with the rules that matched, list every invoice once with whether it is a candidate and whether it is held for review and why, and keep every record that cannot be checked visible, as an exception or in an explicit run failure, so no invoice is lost, counted twice or silently cleared.
recipes.pitch: Catch suspected duplicate supplier invoices before they are paid, with the rule behind every match and a hold list the team can act on.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
Produces a candidate and hold list; it does not block, release or post anything in the payables or payment system.
Stops at duplicate candidates; purchase order matching, recovering paid duplicates and supplier clean-up are separate.
Results as known on a past date need entry timestamps or kept snapshots of the results.
Past hold lists are not kept; a rule or list change restates every result.
recipes.title: Detect duplicate invoice candidates from explicit matching rules before payment
trigger: Accounts payable paid the same supplier invoice twice and only found out when the supplier returned the money.
Before each payment run, accounts payable wants the suspected duplicate invoices to hold for review, with the rule that flagged each one.
The payables system only catches an exact repeat of the invoice number, so re-keyed numbers and invoices entered under a second supplier record slip through.

recipes.description: Build asset-period movements for cost and accumulated depreciation under the approved policies, roll them up to parent, class, entity and total without counting a component twice, reconcile net book value forward, set closing balances beside the ledger, and keep every unprocessable event or unpoliced asset visible or counted, or fail the run naming it, as approved.
recipes.pitch: Turn asset events and approved policies into a register and net-book-value roll-forward that foot each period of a completed run and sit beside the ledger.
qualifiers: Needs dated asset events and ledger balances; policies and their assignments may be captured as editable data.
Takes capitalisation decisions as given; depreciation policy choices follow the approved rules.
Keeps each currency separate; where translation is approved it needs supplied dated rates, else it is unproven.
Placing late changes by recorded date needs one on the events; otherwise restatement is reported unproven.
One book per run; impairment, revaluation, merges, splits, lease accounting and tax books are separate and set aside.
Stops at the register, roll-forward and ledger comparison; break classes, close packs and postings are separate.
recipes.title: Build a fixed-asset register and reconcile its net-book-value roll-forward
trigger: Every month someone rebuilds the fixed-asset register and depreciation schedule in a spreadsheet to prove that opening value plus additions less depreciation and disposals equals closing value.
A partial disposal, a transfer between entities or a cost adjustment leaves the register, the roll-forward and the ledger disagreeing, and nobody can say which asset moved what.
An auditor asks why a class's or an entity's closing net book value, or its difference from the ledger, changed between two periods.

recipes.description: At the approved reconciliation grain, including legal entity and currency where relevant, set the general-ledger balance beside its subledger balance, explain the difference as breaks classed under approved rules, leave any residual visible as unexplained, and keep unprocessable records visible as exceptions, so no amount is lost, counted twice or absorbed.
recipes.pitch: Reconcile every control account to its subledger with each break classified and nothing quietly absorbed.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
Linking breaks to documents needs a document reference on ledger lines or an approved matching rule.
Reproducing a past tie-out after rule or source changes needs kept history of the tie-out.
Stops at the classified tie-out; correcting postings, sign-off and close packs are separate outcomes.
recipes.title: Tie the general ledger to its subledgers and classify every break
trigger: Month-end close stalls because control accounts do not agree with their subledgers and the difference is worked out by hand in a spreadsheet.
The controller will not sign off until every control-account difference is explained, from late postings to manual journals, with nothing left unexplained.
An auditor asks why a control account differed from its subledger at a past period end, and someone has to rebuild the explanation by hand.

recipes.description: Explain the gross-margin change between two periods under the user's approved method as price, unit cost, volume and mix components plus any new, discontinued, no-quantity, interaction, translation, period-length or late-change components the approved rules define, adding up to the observed change when the bridge closes, with any rounding shown and every line left out accounted for.
recipes.pitch: Show why gross margin moved between two periods, with every component adding up to the change when it closes and nothing hidden in a plug.
qualifiers: Needs sales lines for two comparable periods; lines lacking quantity or cost follow the approved disposition.
Takes line revenue and cost as given; allocating shared charges to lines is a separate outcome.
Explains the margin amount; a margin-rate bridge is a separate outcome.
Keeps each currency and unit of measure separate unless an approved rule applies.
Explains a change between two periods; plan versus actual and forecasting are separate.
Needs dated line, rate and mapping versions to prove a restatement; without them it reads unproven.
Stops at the bridge; commentary, charts and repricing advice are separate outcomes.
recipes.title: Explain gross-margin change with a reconciled price, volume, mix, and cost bridge
trigger: Finance subtracts one period's gross margin from another and writes the explanation by hand, and the story changes with whoever builds it.
Price, volume, mix and cost effects do not add up to the margin change, or an unlabelled line absorbs the difference.
New products, discontinued products, returns or a zero base quantity distort the volume and mix effect and nobody can see by how much.

recipes.description: Schedule each contract line's allocated price by period under the approved recognition rules, net billing against it into deferred revenue or the approved asset or receivable at the approved netting level, roll the positions forward at the approved grain, and keep every unprocessable contract or billing line visible, so no amount is lost, counted twice or recognised early.
recipes.pitch: Turn contracts and invoices into a revenue schedule and a deferred-revenue roll-forward that tie to each other and to every invoice line.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
Needs contract lines carrying their allocated price and dated terms; price allocation is a separate outcome.
Treats each contract line as one performance obligation; combining lines into one obligation is a separate outcome.
On business dates alone, a backdated change restates earlier periods; reproducing them needs kept history.
Stops at the schedule and roll-forward; journal postings, period locking and translation are separate.
recipes.title: Generate the revenue-recognition schedule and deferred-revenue roll-forward from contracts
trigger: Revenue is spread across months by hand in a spreadsheet and never agrees with the deferred revenue balance or with what was invoiced.
Every month-end someone rebuilds the deferred revenue roll-forward and cannot explain its movement contract by contract.
An auditor asks how much of a contract was recognised in each period and why, including after it was upsold, repriced or cancelled part way through.

recipes.description: For each approved scenario version, roll cash forward over thirteen weeks from opening balances and approved open items, payroll and commitments, keeping the date and rule behind every movement and every item left out of the weeks visible with its reason and amount.
recipes.pitch: Roll cash forward week by week for each approved scenario, with the date and rule behind every movement and nothing quietly dropped.
qualifiers: Open items arrive as landed tables; aging them is a separate outcome.
Uses approved assumptions only; it is not a forecasting model or a recommendation to borrow or invest.
Stops at the plan; budget comparison, revaluation and ledger posting are separate outcomes.
A past plan as issued needs kept snapshots; a rebuild restates it.
A calendar or rate the rules need but the source lacks is reported as unproven.
Rates, calendars and rules are inputs; sourcing rates and detecting duplicate invoices are separate outcomes.
recipes.title: Build a thirteen-week cash plan with traceable scenario assumptions
trigger: The weekly cash view is a spreadsheet rebuilt by hand each week, and nobody can say which receipt, payment or assumption moved a week's balance.
Treasury needs a weekly roll-forward for each approved scenario, with the date and rule behind every expected movement, before the cash review.
Overdue invoices, disputed items, undated obligations and invoices listed in two inputs are handled differently by each person who builds the plan.

recipes.description: Build the trial balance by account and fiscal period, plus entity and currency where more than one is in scope, with opening, debits, credits and closing, roll it up to statement lines, list late postings and invalid journals, and record each period's state at or after its hard close so any later change to it is handled as the approved lock policy says.
recipes.pitch: Rebuild the trial balance and close pack every period, with closed periods recorded, later changes caught and every journal accounted for.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
Detecting a change to a closed period needs state that later builds and full refreshes do not rewrite.
Naming a changed line needs stable line ids; lateness and an as-at-hard-close record need posting instants and history.
Stops at the close pack; subledger tie-out, consolidation, FX and posting corrections are separate outcomes.
recipes.title: Produce the trial balance and close pack as code
trigger: The close pack is rebuilt by hand every period and last quarter's trial balance cannot be reproduced as it was when the period closed.
Auditors ask what a closed period showed at its hard close and whether anything was posted into it afterwards.
Controllers need the journals posted after the soft close listed, and a hard stop when a closed period changes.

recipes.description: At the approved grain, assign each billing line to a team, product and environment by its tags, split shared pools by an approved method, keep untagged and unallocated cost visible with its reason, flag daily spikes, and close allocated plus unallocated to each invoice.
recipes.pitch: Show which team drives the cloud bill, with untagged cost kept as untagged and every allocation closing to the invoice.
qualifiers: Billing lines, invoices and tag rules arrive as landed tables; landing a provider export is a separate outcome.
Stops at the allocation; budgets, forecasts, commitment optimisation and chargeback are separate outcomes.
Currency conversion needs an approved rate source; without one, each currency is reported on its own.
Allocation is only as good as the tags and drivers supplied; a wrong but valid tag is not detectable.
recipes.title: Allocate cloud and platform spend to teams and flag untagged cost and daily spikes
trigger: The cloud bill grew and nobody can say which team or product drove the increase.
Untagged spend is unknown, or is quietly spread across teams so that no one owns it.
Shared platform costs are split by a rule nobody can reproduce, and the shares do not add back to the bill.
A daily cost spike is noticed only when the invoice arrives.

recipes.description: For each application and period, compare the seats the contract entitles, the invoice bills and the console assigns with the seats used under an approved activity rule, publish utilisation, unused-seat cost, shelfware and renewal timing, keep person-level idle seats restricted, and account for every record.
recipes.pitch: Measure paid SaaS seats against real use, flag shelfware before renewal, and keep the idle-user list restricted.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
Contract, invoice, assignment and activity records arrive as landed tables; landing them is a separate outcome.
Stops at the utilisation report; renewal terms, deprovisioning and seat reclaim are separate outcomes.
Other plan models (usage-based, unlimited, pooled) need an approved treatment before they count as seats.

Hiding small groups alone does not make a figure safe to release; totals and sibling cells can reveal one.
Unless issued periods are kept as retained copies, a late or backdated event restates the periods it affects.
Vendor activity feeds differ; unless approved otherwise, no feed or a declared gap reads unknown, not inactive.
recipes.title: Measure SaaS licence utilisation and shelfware against contracts and invoices
trigger: A SaaS renewal is due and nobody can say how many of the paid seats are actually used.
The vendor console, the contract and the invoice show different seat counts for the same application.
Finance is asked what the unused seats cost and which applications are shelfware before the renewal date.

recipes.description: Build a dlt pipeline and a governed table that load each new export of a hand-maintained spreadsheet under an approved structure contract, keep the last accepted version live when an export breaks it, set aside bad rows with reasons, retain accepted versions as approved, and document every column with its owner.
recipes.pitch: Turn the spreadsheet everyone depends on into a governed table that fails loudly when its structure breaks.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dlt support and are unassessed.

Covers a delimited text export such as CSV; reading a workbook directly is out of scope.
Sized for spreadsheet-scale files, not large extracts.
Needs a Studio route for dlt to read the file; cloud buckets (ADLS, S3) have none today.
recipes.title: Promote a spreadsheet or CSV to a governed, tested table
trigger: A spreadsheet that reports and models depend on is edited by hand, and a moved, renamed or retyped column keeps breaking them quietly.

A team keeps editing a sheet and re-exporting it, and wants a warehouse table of it that is checked on every new export.

recipes.description: Explain every billed claim line as paid, adjusted, patient responsibility, denied or open so the pieces add up to the billed amount, summarise the same by payer with denial rate and denial reasons, account for every remittance line as applied or set aside with its reason, and tie each remittance batch to its payment.
recipes.pitch: Billed to paid, adjusted, denied and open for every claim line and payer, with every remittance line applied or explained and every batch tied to its payment.

Only as complete as the remittances received; claims not yet remitted are shown as approved.
recipes.title: Reconcile billed claims to payer remittances, denials and batch payments by payer
trigger: The revenue cycle team matches payer remittances to billed claims by hand, and nobody can say, payer by payer, how much of what was billed was paid, adjusted, denied or is still open.

A remittance batch does not match the payment it carries, a remittance names a claim nobody holds, or a billed claim has no remittance yet, and the gap is found only at month end.

recipes.description: Classify every loaded admission as an eligible index admission, an admission excluded for one named reason, or an admission set aside as unusable, link each eligible index to the admission that readmits it, and publish a readmission rate by facility and month that ties back to the cohort.
recipes.pitch: Every admission is an index, excluded for a stated reason or set aside, and the readmission rate ties back to it.
qualifiers: Admissions with patient, facility, dates, type, outcome and planned flag must already be landed as a table.
Stops at the cohort and rate; risk adjustment, cost, root cause and outreach are separate.
Readmissions to facilities missing from the data cannot be seen, and are not claimed absent.
recipes.title: Build a thirty-day readmission cohort with explicit exclusions
trigger: The quality team rebuilds a readmission rate from a spreadsheet each quarter, and nobody can say who was left out of the rate or why.

Deaths, transfers, discharges against medical advice and discharges too recent to have had a full follow-up window sit in the rate, or vanish from it without a trace.

recipes.description: Publish rooms available, sold and occupied, room revenue, occupancy, ADR and RevPAR per property and night from reservation lines and room inventory, with every line counted or set aside with a reason and amendments to closed nights handled visibly as approved.
recipes.pitch: One nightly table of occupancy, ADR and RevPAR that reconciles to every reservation line and rolls up from sums.
qualifiers: Needs reservation lines with a nightly rate and a room inventory per property and night already landed as tables.

Judging a later amendment needs a close per night, from the source or an approved rule.
recipes.title: Build nightly occupancy, ADR and RevPAR by property with closed-night restatements
trigger: Occupancy, ADR and RevPAR differ between reports because each one counts stays, comps, out-of-order rooms and cancellations its own way.
A multi-night stay lands on its check-in day, the checkout day is counted as a night, or a month's ADR is an average of daily ADRs.
A reservation amended after a night closed quietly changes a morning figure that revenue management already acted on.

recipes.description: Resolve customer records from several source systems into one golden record per customer, with a two-way crosswalk, approved match and survivorship rules held as data, golden ids that stay stable across runs, an unresolved list that accounts for every source record, and an optional comparison with a source system's own merge pointers.
recipes.pitch: One customer, one stable id, every source record traced to it and every unresolved one explained.
qualifiers: Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other four Studio targets remain unassessed.
Expects names and addresses already standardized, with a match key, by an earlier standardization step.
Stable golden ids need the id register to persist between runs; a rebuild from scratch reissues them.
Without retained crosswalk history, the crosswalk as it stood on a past run cannot be reconstructed.
recipes.title: Deduplicate customers into a golden record with a source crosswalk
trigger: The same customer exists in several systems under different ids, so customer counts and per-customer revenue are inflated.
Analysts need to trace a golden customer to every source record behind it, and any source record to its golden customer.
Source systems disagree on a customer's name, address or contact details and nobody can say which value wins or why.
Customer ids change from one run to the next when a later record turns out to belong to an existing customer.

recipes.description: Standardize every source record's name and postal address under approved, editable rules, keep the original values beside the standardized ones, mint deterministic match keys that agree exactly when the standardized values agree, and account for every record as standardized or excluded with a reason, without merging records.
recipes.pitch: Give every customer record a clean name, a clean address and a match key you can explain.
qualifiers: Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other four Studio targets remain unassessed.
Addresses are standardized by rule, not verified against a postal service, so deliverability is not checked.
recipes.title: Standardize names and addresses and mint deterministic match keys
trigger: The same customer is written differently across CRM, billing and support, so joins on name or address miss.
A deduplication or golden-record step needs stable, explainable match keys before any fuzzy matching.
Addresses arrive in mixed formats across countries, so reports group the same address several ways.
Match results must be reproducible from run to run, without depending on run order or an external service.

recipes.description: Author a new incremental dbt model with an enforced output contract, then prove that a rerun and a re-delivery of records already applied leave it unchanged under the approved definition, with records the approved rules set aside kept visible.
recipes.pitch: Build an incremental dbt model with an enforced contract and show that a rerun or a re-delivery of records already applied leaves it unchanged.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
Needs a source that carries a key and a version or update timestamp for each record, and can be read in full.
Converting an existing full-refresh model belongs to the dbt-full-refresh-to-incremental Recipe.
recipes.title: Author an incremental dbt model with its contract and prove idempotency
trigger: A new dbt model must be brought up to date incrementally on each run, and nobody can show that a rerun or a re-delivery of records already applied leaves it unchanged.
Downstream consumers need a guaranteed set of columns, types and keys, and a build should fail when the output drifts from them.
A loader resends or corrects records, and the table must stay correct when the same batch is delivered twice.

recipes.description: Publish paid and incurred loss triangles by accident period and development age, one per segment, each cell as known at its evaluation date, with every claim transaction counted in a cell or set aside with its reason and the totals tied back to the inputs.
recipes.pitch: Reproducible paid and incurred triangles whose older diagonals never move, with every claim transaction counted or explained.
qualifiers: Claims and claim transactions must already be landed as tables with the dates the approved time basis needs.
Amount triangles only; claim counts, factors, IBNR, ultimates, reserving and reinsurance cessions are separate.
Results are only as complete as the transaction history the source carries; earlier history is not recoverable here.
recipes.title: Build paid and incurred claims loss triangles by accident and development period
trigger: Reserving analysts rebuild loss triangles by hand in spreadsheets, and a late payment or reserve change pushes back into cells that were already reported.
Two runs of the same claims data give different older diagonals, so development methods run on numbers nobody can reproduce.
Incurred is read with today's case reserve instead of the reserve as it stood at each evaluation date, and nobody can say which claim transactions a triangle left out.

recipes.description: From observed receipts, production runs that consume and make lots, and shipments, build the lot genealogy with quantities and units on each link, and for a recalled lot list every affected lot and shipment once with the recalled quantity, with unreconciled runs, cycles and untraceable shipments shown.
recipes.pitch: Trace a recalled lot to every affected shipment once, and show unreconciled runs and shipments whose history cannot be followed.
qualifiers: Needs observed genealogy, such as lots consumed and produced per run; links are never inferred from dates.
Lots follow one identification scheme; mapping between schemes is a separate outcome.
Inputs are landed tables; loading files or extracts belongs to file-drop-to-bronze.
Stops at recall exposure evidence; notifying customers and the physical recall are separate outcomes.
Stock positions and product hierarchies belong to ops-inventory-reconciliation and master-product-sku-hierarchy.
recipes.title: Trace a recalled input lot to affected shipments and flag unreconciled runs and lineage that cannot be traced
trigger: A raw material lot is recalled and nobody can say which finished lots and which customer shipments contain it, or how much of it each holds.
Lot genealogy lives in spreadsheets or separate receipt, production and shipping systems, and a split or blend makes the same material reach a shipment by several routes.
A mock recall must show every affected shipment, and every shipment whose history cannot be followed.

recipes.description: Under one approved costing policy and reporting currency, value each stock movement in a ledger, publish closing stock and cost of goods sold by approved period, keep quantity and value conserved, and list what cannot be valued instead of costing it at zero.
recipes.pitch: Value every stock movement and cost of goods sold under one approved costing policy, with no missing cost quietly becoming zero.
qualifiers: Inputs are landed stock-movement tables; loading files or extracts belongs to file-drop-to-bronze.
One costing policy and one reporting currency per run; currency conversion is upstream work.
Stops at valued inventory and COGS; counts, stockout risk and ledger posting are separate outcomes.
Restating for a backdated movement needs an entry or posting time on each movement; without it restatement is unproven.
Net realisable value write-downs are a separate outcome.
recipes.title: Value inventory movements, closing stock and cost of goods sold under an approved costing policy
trigger: Finance cannot say what closing inventory is worth or how much cost of goods sold a month carries because receipts, issues, returns and adjustments are costed by hand.
A late or backdated receipt arrives and nobody can say which issues, periods and cost figures it changes.
The books are about to close and a missing cost, a return or an issue beyond stock on hand has quietly become zero in the valuation.

recipes.description: Bring a legacy SQL script or view into dbt as models that publish the same contract, proven against the legacy logic's own output on the same inputs, with legacy defects reproduced and reported as follow-up work.

recipes.description: Compute fully loaded acquisition cost, customers acquired and cumulative contribution by acquisition cohort and channel under the user's approved rules, with a payback verdict per cohort and every cost and customer accounted for.

recipes.description: Bind every source item to at most one conformed product and SKU or list why not, map each source category into the approved conformed hierarchy with each product placed at most once per view or listed unplaced, and tie item counts and units to each source at every level with every difference explained or marked not tied.

A stale source must stop the work that depends on it before it rebuilds, and say which source is late, by how much and against what limit.

recipes.description: Convert a Spark ingestion notebook into an owned dlt pipeline that lands beside the notebook's tables, reloads an already-loaded, unchanged file without duplicating, losing or changing a record beyond its load-time and bookkeeping columns, accounts for every source record and every notebook step, and is reconciled table by table with a cause for every difference.
recipes.pitch: Turn a Spark ingestion notebook into a dlt pipeline you own, and prove table by table what it lands and why any row differs.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dlt support and are unassessed.
Needs the notebook's code, the tables it landed, and read access to the files it reads.
Needs a Studio route for dlt to read the notebook's source files; cloud buckets (ADLS, S3) have none today.
recipes.title: Convert a Spark ingestion notebook into a dlt pipeline and reconcile what it lands
trigger: A Spark notebook lands raw files into bronze, and the team wants that load as tested pipeline code without keeping a cluster for it.
An ingestion notebook nobody can change safely mixes parsing, renames and deduplication in cells with no tests, and reruns surprise people.
Models read the tables a Spark notebook lands, so a replacement has to land data they can keep using and account for every difference before anyone switches.

recipes.description: Move a stored procedure that maintains a table run after run into dbt, with each procedural step that shapes the table mapped to a dbt equivalent and parity with the unchanged procedure shown after every compared run, procedure defects reproduced and reported, and retirement only as approved.
recipes.pitch: Retire a stored procedure by rebuilding it in dbt and proving the table matches after every compared run, not only at the end.
qualifiers: Not yet assessed end to end on fabric_warehouse or redshift.
Needs the procedure's table after each compared run, from the unchanged procedure or approved snapshots.
Views and one-shot scripts that rebuild their whole output each run belong to the legacy-sql-to-dbt Recipe.
Procedures that keep row history, such as hand-rolled slowly changing dimensions, are out of scope.
Applies when the maintained table is the required outcome and all relevant behaviour is represented through its state.
recipes.title: Convert a stored procedure into a dbt model and prove parity
trigger: A nightly load is a stored procedure nobody fully understands, and it inserts, updates, deletes or merges rows in a table people depend on.
The team wants the procedure's logic in dbt with tests and lineage, but consumers need proof the table ends up the same after every run.
A procedure that maintains a table in place has to move into the dbt project before it can be retired.

recipes.description: Land switch call-detail batches with their manifests, report every expected batch against its declared count, and publish usage per subscriber and day with each day's backing stated, every record counted or set aside with a reason, and late batches restated visibly.
recipes.pitch: Land call-detail batches and publish subscriber-day usage with batch completeness, day backing and visible restatement of late batches.
qualifiers: Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; other listed targets rely on dlt and dbt support and are unassessed.
Needs a Studio route for dlt to read the drop; cloud buckets (ADLS, S3) have none today.
Needs each batch to arrive with a manifest stating its declared record count, or the batch cannot be judged.
Needs a source of expected batches; a batch neither expected nor delivered cannot be seen.
Covers delimited text batches such as CSV; other layouts are out of scope.
Stops at subscriber-day usage; rating, billing, churn, ARPU, fraud and network quality are separate work.
Landing controls for layout, rescans and part-way failure follow file-drop-to-bronze.
A generic file drop with no usage rollup belongs to file-drop-to-bronze.
recipes.title: Land call-detail batches and aggregate them into subscriber-day usage with manifest completeness
trigger: Monthly subscriber usage differs by who ran it, because nobody can say which call-detail batches had landed or whether each arrived complete.
A batch is re-sent, cut short, missing its manifest or delivered late, and the usage numbers change or hold a quiet day that was really a gap.
Billing or network analytics need usage per subscriber per day with every record accounted for and each day marked as backed by complete batches or not.

recipes.description: Turn usage events, with repeats and revisions resolved under approved rules, and approved contract terms into charge lines per customer, period, meter and currency with allowance, tier method and credits applied, every event accounted for, and corrections restated for only the affected scope.
recipes.pitch: Rate usage under approved allowances, tiers and credits so every event is accounted for and a correction restates only what it touches.
qualifiers: Usage events must already be landed as tables; ingesting them is a separate outcome.
Needs approved terms per customer and meter; they may be captured as editable data during the run.
Keeps each currency separate; conversion is a separate outcome.
Restating earlier results needs the figures as last reported to be kept between runs.
Stops at rated usage lines; fixed fees, minimum charges, invoices, payments, tax and revenue recognition are separate.
A flat dated rate with no period-wide allowance or tiers belongs to effective-dated-business-rules.
recipes.title: Calculate rated usage charges with allowances, tiers, credits and restated corrections
trigger: Usage charges differ by who calculated them, because graduated and volume pricing, shared allowances and credits are applied differently from one run to the next.
A redelivered event spends a shared allowance twice, or a late, revised or cancelled event forces a rerun of every customer.
Billing or finance needs each customer's charge per period and meter with every usage event rated or set aside, and a change to an earlier period shown as a restatement.

recipes.description: Set metered energy beside billed energy for every in-scope service point and billing period, give each period one verdict under approved tolerance rules, quantify unbilled energy to an approved as-of date, and account for every read and bill line, with no missing read treated as zero.
recipes.pitch: Match metered to billed energy for every in-scope period and quantify what was never billed, with nothing silently dropped.
qualifiers: Reads, a meter master and bill lines must already be landed as tables, with periods from a calendar or approved source.
Quantities only; tariffs, pricing and revenue accruals in money are separate outcomes.
Energy commodities only; volume-only commodities such as water are a separate outcome.
Stops at the classified reconciliation; correcting bills and estimating missing reads are separate.
Reproducing a past as-of date after rule or source changes needs kept history of the sources.
recipes.title: Reconcile meter reads to bills and quantify unbilled energy
trigger: Revenue assurance compares metered usage with billed usage in a spreadsheet each month, and nobody can say which differences are real and which are timing, estimates or a meter swap.
A meter with a multiplier, a register that rolled over or a meter exchanged mid-period makes billed energy disagree with the reads, and the cause is found by hand.
Finance asks how much energy was delivered but never billed, and the answer changes with every join, because a period with no read or no bill looks like zero.

recipes.description: Build a breaking change to a relation's grain, column meaning or shape as a new version beside an unchanged old one, with a change record, revised queries for a bounded set of named consumers and observable criteria for retiring the old version.
recipes.pitch: Build a breaking change as a new version beside the old one, with named consumers revised and checked and retirement left as stated criteria.
qualifiers: A compatible type correction or one compatible rename belongs to an existing Feature, not to this Recipe.
Consumers are the bounded set the owner names; deployment and retirement belong to the existing harness.
recipes.title: Add a breaking data contract change as a new version beside the old one and revise its named consumers
trigger: A required change to a published relation's grain, column meaning or shape cannot keep the old interface.
Known consumers cannot all switch on the same day and must keep working while they move.
Someone must say what changed, what each reader has to do and when the old version can be retired.
A reader that treats the new version as if it had the old grain would quietly get a wrong answer.
